coding_walkthrough.description: Talking through how to solve a coding problem, out loud.

design_discussion.description: Describing how a system fits together and the choices weighed.

past_example.description: Telling a real example from the person's own work.

case_discussion.description: Structuring and reasoning through a business problem, including rough numbers.

workplace_scenario.description: Explaining how the person would handle a described work situation.

templates.fallback: Status updates for parcels can arrive late or twice. Talk me through how you would keep only the newest status for each parcel.
You have a very long list of log lines and little memory. How would you find which messages repeat most often, and what would you trade off?
Walk me through how you would merge several already ordered streams of events into one ordered stream, and how the cost grows as streams are added.
Explain how you would spot that two entries in a large contact list are the same person when their names are spelled differently.
Pick one piece of code you wrote that had a tricky edge case. Explain the case and how you made sure it was handled.
templates.story_text: In “{story}”, pick one piece of logic with a tricky edge case. Explain the case and how you made sure your code handled it.

templates.fallback: Talk me through how you would choose a data structure for a lookup that also needs every key between two values.
How would you order a set of jobs that depend on each other, and what would you do if the dependencies formed a loop?
You have just written a small function. Which inputs would you try first before handing it over, and why those?
Given a sequence of daily readings, how would you find the highest total across any fixed-length run of days? Explain how you would avoid rescanning each run.
A calendar contains many time intervals. How would you find whether any two overlap, and how would your approach change if you needed every overlapping pair?
A function receives a date and amount as text. How would you handle values it cannot use and explain the result to its caller?
Choose an algorithm you know well. Explain its running time to a teammate, including what input characteristic makes the work grow.
Design a service that lets shop owners schedule price changes for a future time. What are the main parts, and what happens if the scheduler falls behind?
Sketch a system that sends order updates to millions of phones. Where would messages wait, and how would you stop the same update arriving twice?
Think of a system you worked on. What would break first if usage grew ten times, and what would you change?
templates.story_text: In “{story}”, what would break first if usage grew ten times, and what would you change?

templates.fallback: Design a booking system for a small chain of clinics. How would you stop two people booking the same slot?
Design a service that shows which delivery vans are near each depot right now. How often would you update positions, and why?
How would you design a list of recent activity for each user, and what would you prepare ahead of time versus build when asked?
Design a service for uploading large files over an unreliable connection. How would clients resume, and how would you confirm the finished file?
A finance team needs a searchable history of every change to an account. How would you store and retrieve that history without losing earlier versions?
Design a daily email digest for millions of users across time zones. How would you schedule delivery and handle a slow mail provider?
How would you release a new feature to a small share of users first, observe its impact, and quickly stop the rollout if problems appear?
Design inventory reservations for an online store so abandoned checkouts eventually release stock without overselling it.
Design search suggestions that appear as someone types. How would you keep suggestions useful while updating them as popular searches change?
A photo-sharing app needs thumbnails in several sizes. How would uploads be processed if image conversion can take time or cannot be completed?
Pick one design choice you would make for a busy online shop and explain it to someone who has never built a large system.
Tell me about a time you shipped something under a deadline that was not as complete as you wanted. What did you leave out, and what did you do afterwards?
Tell me about a time you noticed a problem outside your own task and decided to act on it.
Tell me about a time a user's need changed how you built something.
Tell me about a decision at work that was yours alone. What did you weigh up before making it?
templates.story_text: In “{story}”, which decision was yours alone, and what did you weigh up before making it?

templates.fallback: Tell me about a time you dug into the details to understand why something kept breaking.
Tell me about a time you and a teammate disagreed about a technical choice. How did you settle it?
Tell me about a time you made something simpler for the people who had to use it.
Tell me about a time you held your own work to a higher standard than anyone asked for. What did that cost, and was it worth it?
Tell me about a time a plan you owned stopped working. How did you respond, and what did you learn?
Tell me about feedback that changed how you work. What did you do differently afterwards?
Tell me about a time you helped a teammate succeed when it was not part of your assigned work.
Tell me about a piece of work whose outcome surprised you. How did you determine whether it had helped?
A chain of neighbourhood cafés has seen profit fall for three quarters while sales stayed flat. How would you structure your first look at why?
Roughly how many bicycle repairs happen in a year in a city of two million people? Talk through your assumptions and how you would check the answer feels sensible.
Patients at a group of clinics now wait far longer than last year. How would you break down where the delay comes from before suggesting any fix?
A grocery delivery firm wants to start in a new city. What would you need to know before recommending yes or no, and in what order would you find it out?
A subscription business is thinking of raising its price by ten percent. How would you judge whether that is a good idea?
Sales rose by a fifth while product returns doubled. Explain how you would work out whether the business is actually doing better.
A logistics company wants to cut its costs by fifteen percent without slowing deliveries. How would you organise the problem before looking at any numbers?
You have five minutes left with someone who wants one recommendation from your work. How would you sum it up, and which risk would you mention?
A gym has the same fixed costs each month and charges every member the same fee. Walk me through how you would find how many members it needs to break even.
A bank has money for only two of six improvement projects. How would you decide which two to fund, and what would make you change your mind?
A call centre gets about nine hundred calls on a busy day. Talk me through how you would estimate how many people it needs on shift.
Think of a problem you worked on where your first answer did not hold up. How did you structure it the second time?
templates.story_text: In “{story}”, how did you break the problem into parts, and what would you check first if you did it again?

templates.fallback: A manager asks for a dashboard that shows how the team is doing. What questions would you ask before writing any requirements?
Two department heads want opposite changes to the same approval process. How would you move them towards one decision?
Halfway through a project, the sponsor keeps adding small requests. How would you handle them without losing the sponsor's support?
Describe how you would map the current steps of an invoice approval process that nobody has ever written down.
A team will build a feature that lets customers change a delivery address. How would you write acceptance criteria that testers can check?
Explain how you would present a delayed project to a senior leader who has two minutes and needs to know what to decide.
The report your stakeholders rely on uses data you suspect is incomplete. What would you do before the next review meeting?
The people who will use a new system say the old way works fine. How would you understand and respond to their concerns?
You have twenty requested changes and time for five. How would you decide, and how would you explain the choice to the people left out?
A project changes hands next week. What would you write down so the new team understands what was agreed and why?
A client expects a feature next month that will not be ready in time. How would you prepare for and run that conversation?
Tell me about a time someone you worked with disagreed with your recommendation. How did you handle it?
templates.story_text: In “{story}”, who disagreed with you or needed convincing, and how did you handle it?

templates.fallback: Tell me about a time you had to deliver a report or set of findings under a tight deadline. What did you leave out, and why?
Tell me about a time you started a piece of work with very little direction. How did you decide what to do first?
Tell me about a time people in your team disagreed on how to proceed. What part did you play in settling it?
Tell me about a mistake in your own work that someone else noticed. What did you do next?
Tell me about a time you persuaded someone more senior than you to change their mind.
Tell me about a time you had to learn an unfamiliar subject quickly to get your work done.
Tell me about a decision in a project that was yours to make. What did you weigh up before making it?
templates.story_text: In “{story}”, which decision was yours to make, and what did you weigh up first?

templates.fallback: Tell me about feedback from a client, user or manager that changed how you work.
Tell me about a time you helped a group succeed with work that was not assigned to you.
Tell me about a time two people needed your help on the same day. How did you decide what came first?
Tell me about a time you made a process easier for the people who had to follow it.
Tell me about a piece of work where you could show the difference it made. How did you measure it?
